title: Object Manager (Slotted Page)
overview:
In this project you will implement the **Object Manager**, which handles variable-length record storage within fixed-size pages using a **slotted page** layout.

A slotted page divides each 4 KB page into three regions: a header (tracking the number of slots and free space offset), a slot array (growing forward from the header), and record data (growing backward from the end of the page). This design allows efficient insertion and deletion of variable-length records without external fragmentation.

You will also implement **serialization** and **deserialization** of database rows (a map of column names to typed values) into compact byte arrays suitable for disk storage.

tasks.title: Slotted Page Operations
tasks.description:
The slotted page layout within a `DB_PAGE_SIZE` (4096 byte) page:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐  offset 0
│ PageHeader: num_slots(2B) | free_off(2B)│
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤  offset 4
│ SlotInfo[0]: offset(2B) | length(2B)    │
│ SlotInfo[1]: offset(2B) | length(2B)    │
│ ...                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│           Free Space                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Records (grow downward from page end)   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘  offset 4096
```

Slots with `offset=0, length=0` are considered deleted. No compaction is required.

functions.name: InsertRecord(page_id_t page_id, const vector<uint8_t>& record) → slot_id_t
functions.description: Insert a serialized record into the specified page. Calculate the available free space as: `free_space_offset - PAGE_HEADER_SIZE - (num_slots * SLOT_INFO_SIZE)`. If the record plus a new slot entry won't fit, return `INVALID_SLOT_ID`. Otherwise, write the record at `free_space_offset - record.size()`, add a new slot entry, and update the header.
hints: Fetch the page via `buffer_manager_->FetchPage(page_id)`.
Read the header with `ReadHeader(data)` (provided helper).
Free space = `header.free_space_offset - PAGE_HEADER_SIZE - num_slots * SLOT_INFO_SIZE`.
Check: `record.size() + SLOT_INFO_SIZE <= free_space`.
Write record at offset `header.free_space_offset - record.size()`.
Unpin the page as dirty after modifying.

functions.name: DeleteRecord(page_id_t page_id, slot_id_t slot_id)
functions.description: Delete a record by setting its slot's offset and length to 0. The space is not reclaimed (no compaction). Simply invalidate the slot entry.
hints: Read the slot with `ReadSlot()`, set both fields to 0, write back with `WriteSlot()`.

functions.name: GetRecord(page_id_t page_id, slot_id_t slot_id) → vector<uint8_t>
functions.description: Retrieve a record's bytes from the given page and slot. Throw `RecordNotFoundException` if the slot index is out of range or the slot has been deleted (length == 0).
hints: Read the slot info. Check `slot_id < num_slots` and `slot.length > 0`.
Copy `length` bytes from `data + offset`.

functions.name: GetRecordCount(page_id_t page_id) → uint16_t
functions.description: Count the records still live in a page. A slot whose length is 0 was deleted and does not count.
hints: Fetch the page and read `num_slots` from the header.
Count the slots whose length is above 0.
Unpin the page — you did not change it.

functions.name: GetFreeSpace(page_id_t page_id) → uint16_t
functions.description: How many bytes a new record could still use in this page: the gap between the end of the slot directory and the start of the record area.
hints: The directory ends at `PAGE_HEADER_SIZE + num_slots * SLOT_INFO_SIZE`.
The record area starts at `free_space_offset`.
Unpin the page — you did not change it.

tasks.title: Row Serialization
tasks.description:
Serialize and deserialize `Row` objects (an `unordered_map<string, Value>`) into compact byte arrays. The serialization format follows **schema column order** — this is critical for consistent encoding/decoding.

For each column in the schema:
```
[type_tag: 1 byte] [data: variable]
  INTEGER → 4 bytes (int32_t, little-endian)
  FLOAT   → 8 bytes (double)
  BOOLEAN → 1 byte (0 or 1)
  STRING  → 4 bytes (uint32_t length) + N bytes (character data)
```

functions.name: SerializeRow(const Row& row, const Schema& schema) → vector<uint8_t>
functions.description: Iterate through `schema.GetColumns()` in order. For each column, look up the value in `row` by column name, write the type tag (the `DataType` enum cast to `uint8_t`), then write the value bytes according to the format above.
hints: Use `reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t*>(&value)` to get raw bytes.
For STRING, write the 4-byte length first, then the character data.
Use `result.insert(result.end(), bytes, bytes + N)` to append bytes.

functions.name: DeserializeRow(const vector<uint8_t>& data, const Schema& schema) → Row
functions.description: Reverse the serialization process. Read column by column in schema order, extracting the type tag and then the appropriately-sized data. Construct `Value` objects and insert them into the result `Row` map.
hints: Track a `pos` index through the data buffer.
Read the type tag first (`data[pos++]`).
Use `memcpy` to read multi-byte values.
Always check bounds before reading (`pos + sizeof(T) <= data.size()`).

breakdown.covers: Insert/get single & multiple, delete, page full, invalid slot
Integer, float, string, empty string, boolean, mixed types, roundtrip

testing.note: Project #1 ships inside this download as a compiled reference library, so your buffer manager works correctly no matter how your own Project #1 went. Nothing to turn on — `cmake -B build` picks it up.
testing.platforms: macOS or Linux, on either Intel or ARM. On Windows, build inside WSL: a native Windows toolchain is refused, because the reference libraries these downloads carry are built for macOS and Linux only.

hints: Draw the slotted page layout on paper and trace through an insertion step by step.
Remember: records grow downward (from DB_PAGE_SIZE toward 0), slots grow upward (from the header).
The free space is the gap between the last slot entry and the first record.
For serialization, use `schema.GetColumns()` to guarantee consistent column ordering.
Test serialization/deserialization independently before combining with InsertRecord/GetRecord.
Use the provided `ReadHeader`/`WriteHeader`/`ReadSlot`/`WriteSlot` helpers — don't manually compute byte offsets.

submission.where: Upload the archive to PLMS (https://plms.postech.ac.kr) under Project #2 before the deadline. Submissions sent by email, or left anywhere else, are not collected.
submission.note: Keep the original directory layout inside the archive (src/…), so the files drop straight back into the project tree. Submit only the files you edited: no build/ directory, no compiled objects, no reference libraries.

blocks.text: **For each module below, write one expression that is always true of it** — true before any of its functions is called, and true again every time one of them returns. It may go false in the middle of a function; that is what makes it worth writing down.
The expression is symbols, not words:
If something is hard to put in symbols, define it as a variable in words, then use the variable in the expression:

code: P = the spaces with a car in them
F = the spaces that are empty
for i in 0 .. total_spaces-1:  i in P or i in F

blocks.text: A module holds several such expressions true at once. Pick one and get it right; you do not have to find them all.
**For each function you wrote, show your expression is still true when it returns.** A line or two each, grouped by module.
If a function cannot affect the expression, say so in one line. If it could, say which step keeps it true.
